symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the source vector, a count.
symbols.quote: The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the target vector, a count.
symbols.quote: The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

symbols.name: relative excess
symbols.meaning: The relative excess $t/s-1$ of the target length over the source length.
symbols.quote: Let $\theta = t/s-1$ be the relative excess of $t$ over $s$.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.quote: Here $u$ is a vector of $s$ coordinates and $v$ a vector of $t$ coordinates.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.quote: Here $u$ is a vector of $s$ coordinates and $v$ a vector of $t$ coordinates.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on length-$s$ vectors with $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$.
symbols.quote: Its permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices: $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on length-$t$ vectors with $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$.
symbols.quote: Its permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices: $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$.

symbols.name: precision
symbols.meaning: The integer precision of the numerical approximation.
symbols.quote: The identity needs $\theta > p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha \ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width (a larger $\alpha$ gives wider weights below) and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: An integer at least 2 setting the width of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The identity needs $\theta > p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha \ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width (a larger $\alpha$ gives wider weights below) and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

symbols.name: Gaussian map S
symbols.meaning: The map from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors with Gaussian weights $e^{-\pi\alpha^{-2}(j-sk/t)^2}$.
symbols.quote: $S$ maps vectors of $s$ coordinates to vectors of $t$ coordinates by $(Su)_k=\frac{1}{\alpha}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{-2}(j-sk/t)^2}u_j$, and $T$ maps them by $(Tu)_k=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{2}(tj/s-k)^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: Gaussian map T
symbols.meaning: The map from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors with Gaussian weights $e^{-\pi\alpha^{2}(tj/s-k)^2}$.
symbols.quote: $S$ maps vectors of $s$ coordinates to vectors of $t$ coordinates by $(Su)_k=\frac{1}{\alpha}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{-2}(j-sk/t)^2}u_j$, and $T$ maps them by $(Tu)_k=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{2}(tj/s-k)^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: nearest target index
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest to $tj/s$, for each $j<s$.
symbols.quote: $C$ selects, for each $j<s$, the entry of a length-$t$ vector at $m_j$, the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map selecting, for each $j<s$, the entry of a length-$t$ vector at $m_j$.
symbols.quote: $C$ selects, for each $j<s$, the entry of a length-$t$ vector at $m_j$, the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

symbols.name: correction diagonal
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on length-$s$ vectors that cancels the Gaussian factor of $T$ at the selected entry.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map $(Du)_j = e^{\pi\alpha^2(tj/s-m_j)^2}u_j$ on length-$s$ vectors, which cancels the Gaussian factor of $T$ at that entry.

symbols.name: correction map
symbols.meaning: The map $CTD$ on length-$s$ vectors, close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Put $N = CTD$, the correction map on length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The map that leaves every vector unchanged.
symbols.quote: Here $I$ is the identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.

symbols.name: scaled diagonal
symbols.quote: Write $D'=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}D$ for the scaled diagonal map.

symbols.name: first contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction $S/2$, from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors.
symbols.quote: Set $A = S/2$ and $B_0 = 2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$, where $A$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors and $B_0$ maps back.

symbols.name: second contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction $2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$, from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors.
symbols.quote: Set $A = S/2$ and $B_0 = 2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$, where $A$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors and $B_0$ maps back.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling is an identity that replaces the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of an arbitrary length by transforms whose lengths are powers of two.
It serves the [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of digit vectors, which needs such transforms.
The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.
Its permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices: $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$.
The size of $N-I$ is measured by its [operator norm](operator-norm.md), $\|N-I\|$, and the sources bound it by $2^{-\alpha^2\theta}$.
